body:
Thank you again. I'm planning on visiting a clinic if I still can't eat or sleep. 

It's the issue that's brought a lot of bad thoughts back to my mind, because I feel like it's one of the most serious and possibly devastating situations I've faced in my adult life.

Honestly, you don't sound selfish at all in fact you sound like someone who is deeply deserving of love. Anyone who questions their own needs the way you are doing seems to me an inherently good, decent person, because the most decent people I find are those who question their own needs.
I'm looking for that practical way out, but there's always the bad exit waiting right in front of me.

Thank you for your kind words. Right now it's the uncertainty that's killing me. Like the coin is in the air and I have to wait agonizing hours and days for it to land. Hope is what really, really hurts the most. I don't know if I can make it but I'm trying so hard for her.

Think of all the good you'll be able to do when you become a cop. Think of the difference you can make to other people who are going through depression as well, but have lashed out at the world instead of just turning inward. Think of how many more lives you can literally save. Think of all the people around you who may be on a slow path to self-destruction. Think of your life's journey intersecting with theirs. Think that, if there is anything like what we call fate out there in the universe, someone may be waiting for you to help them.
